headline: Learning Science Over Panic
thesis: From bans and pauses to tech sovereignty, this week's coverage argues that AI decisions should follow learning evidence, not fear or vendor momentum.
summary: EdSurge and Inside Higher Ed both landed on the same point today: start from how students learn. EdSurge argues that banning AI pushes use onto personal devices and that schools should build skills first, while Inside Higher Ed's opinion pages call for learning science to guide AI choices and ask whether tech sovereignty can reduce Big Tech dependence. The University of Maryland trial (about 15% usage) and an employer survey showing degrees gaining value keep the focus on proof. EdTech Magazine's human-centered IT piece, Ed-Fi's statewide data stories and 1EdTech's November webinars round out the people and data side. Several sources had nothing dated today and show recent or evergreen items.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · OCTOBER 27, 2026 · Search-snippet based; several sources had no items dated today and show recent or evergreen content.

themes.title: Security & Privacy

themes.title: People & Skills

themes.title: Platforms & Sovereignty
